=== comments and labels
; a comment line
LABEL1:	MOV.L	[R1], R2	; Example of a mnemonic.
	NOP
--- gnu
LABEL1:	mov.l	[r1], r2
	nop
=== numbers: B, O and H suffixes, and decimal
	.LWORD	1011000B, 1011000b, 60702O, 60702o, 9243
	.LWORD	0A5FH, 5FH, 0a5fh, 5fh, 0FFFFFF81H
--- gnu
	.long	88, 88, 25026, 25026, 9243
	.long	0xa5f, 0x5f, 0xa5f, 0x5f, 0xffffff81
=== characters and strings in .BYTE
	.BYTE	"abcd", 'x', "A", 1, 2, 3
--- gnu
	.byte	0x61, 0x62, 0x63, 0x64, 0x78, 0x41, 1, 2, 3
=== widths of .BYTE, .WORD and .LWORD
	.BYTE	0FFH, -1
	.WORD	1, 1234H
	.LWORD	11111111H, 22222222H
--- gnu
	.byte	0xff, 0xff
	.short	1, 0x1234
	.long	0x11111111, 0x22222222
=== operator precedence: shifts below `+`, `&` above `|` and `^`
	.LWORD	1+2<<1, 2&1+1, 6|1^3, 1<<2+1, 7&3|8
	.LWORD	10%4*2, ~0&0FFH, 2+3*4, 16>>2-1, -(3-5)
--- gnu
	.long	6, 2, 4, 8, 11
	.long	4, 255, 14, 8, 2
=== .EQU symbols in operands and expressions
symbol	.EQU	1
symbol1	.EQU	symbol+symbol
CNT	.EQU	0FFH
	MOV.L	#symbol1, R1
	MOV.L	#CNT, R2
	ADD	#symbol+2, R3
--- gnu
	mov.l	#2, r1
	mov.l	#0xff, r2
	add	#3, r3
=== names with `$`, `_` and `.`
	.GLB	name1, name2
	.GLB	name4
lab$1:	NOP
_x.y:	NOP
	BRA	lab$1
	BRA	_x.y
--- gnu
lab_1:	nop
x_y:	nop
	bra	lab_1
	bra	x_y
=== `$` is the location symbol
	BRA	$
	.LWORD	$-lab
lab:	NOP
--- gnu
	bra	.
here:	.long	here-lab
lab:	nop
=== temporary labels `?:`, `?+` and `?-`
?:
	BRA	?+
	NOP
	NOP
	NOP
?:
	BRA	?-
	BRA	?-
--- gnu
1:
	bra	2f
	nop
	nop
	nop
2:
	bra	2b
	bra	2b
=== size specifiers
	MOV.B	#0, [R3]
	MOV.W	R1, R2
	MOV.L	R1, R2
	mov.b	[r1], r2
	MOVU.W	4[R1], R2
--- gnu
	mov.b	#0, [r3]
	mov.w	r1, r2
	mov.l	r1, r2
	mov.b	[r1], r2
	movu.w	4[r1], r2
=== branch distance specifiers
L0:	BRA.S	L1
	BEQ.S	L1
	NOP
	NOP
L1:	BRA.B	L0
	BRA.W	L0
	BRA.A	L0
	BRA.L	R1
	BSR.W	L0
	BSR.A	L0
	BSR.L	R2
	BNE.W	L0
	BGT.B	L0
	RTS
--- gnu
L0:	bra.s	L1
	beq.s	L1
	nop
	nop
L1:	bra.b	L0
	bra.w	L0
	bra.a	L0
	bra.l	r1
	bsr.w	L0
	bsr.a	L0
	bsr.l	r2
	bne.w	L0
	bgt.b	L0
	rts
=== branches without a specifier take the shortest distance
L0:	BRA	L1
	BEQ	L1
	BNE	L0
	BSR	L0
L1:	RTS
--- gnu
L0:	bra	L1
	beq	L1
	bne	L0
	bsr	L0
L1:	rts
=== the addressing modes of §5.1.5 (2)
	ADD	R1, R2
	ADD	[R1], R2
	ADD	400[R1], R2
	MOV.L	#-100, R2
	RACW	#1
	BSET	#7, R10
	ADD	#15, R8
	BSET	#31, R10
	MOV.L	R3, 124[R1]
	MOV.L	[R3+], R1
	MOV.L	[-R3], R1
	MOV.L	[R3,R1], R2
	MOV.L	R3, [R1,R2]
	MVFC	PSW, R2
	CLRPSW	U
	ADD	[R1].B, R2
	AND	125[R1].UB, R2
	MOV.L	SP, R1
--- gnu
	add	r1, r2
	add	[r1], r2
	add	400[r1], r2
	mov.l	#-100, r2
	racw	#1
	bset	#7, r10
	add	#15, r8
	bset	#31, r10
	mov.l	r3, 124[r1]
	mov.l	[r3+], r1
	mov.l	[-r3], r1
	mov.l	[r3,r1], r2
	mov.l	r3, [r1,r2]
	mvfc	psw, r2
	clrpsw	u
	add	[r1].b, r2
	and	125[r1].ub, r2
	mov.l	r0, r1
=== bit length specifiers naming the shortest form
	MOV.L	#5:4, R1
	MOV.L	#-100:8, R2
	MOV.L	#200 :8, R2
	DIV	#5:8, R1
	ADD	#1000:16, R1
	ADD	#-100000:24, R1
	MOV.L	#12345678H:32, R1
	MOV.B	#200:8, [R1]
	MOV.W	#40000:16, [R1]
	MOV.L	R3, 124:5[R1]
	ADD	400:8[R1], R2
	ADD	4000:16[R1], R2
	MOV.L	#20:8, 4:5[R1]
	BSET	#7:3, [R1].B
	BSET	#31:5, R10
	SHLR	#3:5, R4
	MVTIPL	#9:4
	RACW	#2:1
--- gnu
	mov.l	#5, r1
	mov.l	#-100, r2
	mov.l	#200, r2
	div	#5, r1
	add	#1000, r1
	add	#-100000, r1
	mov.l	#0x12345678, r1
	mov.b	#200, [r1]
	mov.w	#40000, [r1]
	mov.l	r3, 124[r1]
	add	400[r1], r2
	add	4000[r1], r2
	mov.l	#20, 4[r1]
	bset	#7, [r1].b
	bset	#31, r10
	shlr	#3, r4
	mvtipl	#9
	racw	#2
=== bit length specifiers on a folded difference and a symbol
S:	.BYTE	1, 2, 3
E:	MOV.L	#E-S:4, R1
	MOV.L	#ext:32, R2
	ADD	#ext:32, R3
--- gnu
s:	.byte	1, 2, 3
e:	mov.l	#e-s, r1
	mov.l	#ext, r2
	add	#ext, r3
=== substitute register names for the PID function
	MOV.L	__PID_R13, __PID_R1
	ADD	#4, __PID_R15, R6
	MOV.L	4[__PID_R2], R3
--- gnu
	mov.l	r13, r1
	add	#4, r15, r6
	mov.l	4[r2], r3
=== .MACRO with arguments, from the manual's example (page 486)
mac	.MACRO	p1,p2,p3
	.IF ..MACPARA == 3
	.IF 'p1' == 'byte'
	MOV.B #p2,[p3]
	.ELSE
	MOV.W #p2,[p3]
	.ENDIF
	.ELIF ..MACPARA == 2
	.IF 'p1' == 'byte'
	MOV.B #p2,[R3]
	.ELSE
	MOV.W #p2,[R3]
	.ENDIF
	.ELSE
	MOV.W R3,R1
	.ENDIF
	.ENDM
	mac word,10,R3
	mac byte,20
	mac byte
--- gnu
	mov.w	#10, [r3]
	mov.b	#20, [r3]
	mov.w	r3, r1
=== `@` concatenates in a macro body (page 497)
mov_nibble .MACRO p1,src,dest
	MOV.@p1 src,dest
	.ENDM
	mov_nibble W,R1,R2
	mov_nibble L,R3,R4
--- gnu
	mov.w	r1, r2
	mov.l	r3, r4
=== .EXITM and .LOCAL
data1	.MACRO value
	.IF value == 0
	.EXITM
	.ENDIF
	.LOCAL m1
m1:	NOP
	BRA m1
	.ENDM
	data1 0
	data1 1
	data1 2
--- gnu
1:	nop
	bra	1b
2:	nop
	bra	2b
=== .MREPEAT and ..MACREP, from the manual's example (page 490)
mac	.MACRO value,reg
	.MREPEAT value
	MOV.B #0,..MACREP[reg]
	.ENDR
	.ENDM
	mac 3,R3
--- gnu
	mov.b	#0, 1[r3]
	mov.b	#0, 2[r3]
	mov.b	#0, 3[r3]
=== .IF, .ELIF and .ELSE; an undefined symbol is 0
TYPE	.EQU	1
	.IF TYPE==0
	.BYTE "Proto Type Mode"
	.ELIF TYPE>0
	.BYTE "Mass Production Mode"
	.ELSE
	.BYTE "Debug Mode"
	.ENDIF
	.IF UNDEFINED == 0
	NOP
	.ENDIF
	.IF 'A' < 'B'
	RTS
	.ENDIF
--- gnu
	.ascii	"Mass Production Mode"
	nop
	rts
=== .DEFINE replaces a name with a string (page 499)
X_HI	.DEFINE	R1
ARGS	.DEFINE	"#2, R3"
	MOV.L	#0, X_HI
	MOV.L	ARGS
	.IF __RENESAS__ == 1
	NOP
	.ENDIF
--- gnu
	mov.l	#0, r1
	mov.l	#2, r3
	nop
=== .ALIGN pads code with NOP (03H), which GNU as spells as `.skip`
	MOV.L	R1, R2
	.ALIGN	4
	RTS
	.ALIGN	2, FILL=0
	NOP
	RTS
--- gnu
	mov.l	r1, r2
	.skip	4 - (. - P) % 4, 3
	rts
	.skip	(2 - (. - P) % 2) % 2, 3
	nop
	rts
=== .OFFSET pads code with NOP (03H)
	NOP
	.OFFSET	8
	RTS
--- gnu
	nop
	.org	8, 3
	rts
=== .END ends the source
	NOP
	.END
	this is not assembled
--- gnu
	nop
